chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Haydarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Jihad is the best of matters after the obligatory duties."

key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: The obligatory duties (specifically the five pillars or core obligations)

ai.seo_question: What is the rank of jihad in Shia Islam after obligatory prayers and fasting?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), placing jihad as the preeminent deed after the foundational *fara'id* (obligations like prayer and fasting). This ranking underscores its dual nature in Shia tradition as both a collective duty (*fard kifaya*) in times of need and a supreme spiritual struggle, reflecting the Imam's emphasis on active defense of the community alongside ritual piety.
